digest.top_line: PMRT after NAC still has no RCT; MDACC non-randomized series: 10-yr LRR 59% vs 16% with PMRT for ≥4 pN+ (p<0.0001), so decide on clinical stage plus ypN.
digest.tldr: Breast-only day of RT decision talks, all resting on retrospective or subset data: margin re-excision vs boost, Oncotype RS prognostic for LRR (SWOG 8814 MVA HR 2.36) but not an omission tool, and PMRT after NAC keyed to ypN. pCR is prognostic per pt (CTNeoBC EFS HR 0.48) yet a weak trial-level surrogate.

sites.intro: Five talks on breast RT decisions and planning; none adds new randomized data, so read each framework as expert synthesis of retrospective series and trial subsets.

studies.name: Margins: Impact on Local Control, Treatment Options
studies.tldr: Close or positive margins raise in-breast LR; re-excise when young or EIC-positive, accept RT boost alone for focal anterior/posterior margins in older pts.
details: 🔍 Acceptable LR for survival equivalent to mastectomy: 1%/yr, or 10% at 10 yrs

details.text: 🔍 Proposed margin framework: re-excision vs RT boost alone

rows: Generally excise; excluded from most RCTs
Young, little cosmetic cost; definite if <40 yrs + EIC
Older, high systemic risk, or anterior/posterior margin
<40 yrs + EIC; benefit uncertain but probably best
Re-excision <2 mm and declined or inappropriate (BCCA)
Boost only if <50 y or grade 3

details.text: 📊 Fox Chase retrospective, 1262 pts (T1-T2), LR by margin; boost 14 / 18 / 20 Gy for negative / close / positive
📊 EORTC 22881, 251 margin-positive pts, 11 year follow-up: boost dose vs LR and 10-yr fibrosis
📊 EORTC boost trial, negative margins, 5318 pts, at 5 yrs

details: 📊 Post hoc EORTC path review (Jones, JCO 2009), 1616 pts: margin status not significant on MVA for LR
📊 FCCC close/positive anterior or posterior margins, 200 pts: 10-yr actuarial LR 5%, median f/u 7 years

details.text: 📊 Residual disease on re-excision by positive-margin extent (Neuschatz, Cancer 2002)
subdetails: Focal: 30%
Minimal: 45%
Moderate: 70%
Extensive: 85%

details.text: 🔍 Re-excision more strongly recommended (BCCA) when margins positive or <2 mm plus:
subdetails: Age <40 yrs, extensive DCIS (EIC), lobular histology, LVI
No systemic therapy, or low systemic risk
Multiple margins involved, or margin status unknown

details: ⚠️ No RCT of boost vs re-excision; MILAN II (QUART vs TART) is the nearest proxy
⚠️ Close/positive LR figures come from retrospective series with differing margin definitions
⚠️ Slides describe EORTC 22881 as 10 vs 25 Gy, then report a 26 Gy arm; dose label inconsistent in source
studies.significance: The RT trade is boost dose against fibrosis: in EORTC 22881 margin-positive pts, LR was 17.5% with a 10 Gy boost vs 10.8% with 26 Gy, at severe fibrosis 3% vs 14%. That bounds how far a boost can substitute for re-excision, because the dose that closes the LR gap costs the cosmesis BCT is meant to protect.
studies.monday_clinic: In an older woman at high systemic risk with a focally positive anterior (skin-only) or posterior (fascia-only) margin, this supports RT boost without re-excision; it does not extend to women under 40 with EIC, where the talk argues re-excision.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Boost is the RT lever for close or positive margins. In **EORTC 22881** (251 margin-positive pts, 11 year follow-up) the higher boost dose lowered LR but raised **severe fibrosis 14% vs 3%**. With negative margins, boost is reserved for pts **<50 y or grade 3**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Survival equivalence rests on the **6 RCTs** of BCT vs mastectomy (NSABP B06, Milan 1, IGR, NCI-US, Danish, EORTC). The talk predates the SSO-ASTRO **no ink on tumour** consensus for invasive disease, which supersedes the **>2 mm** negative definition used throughout.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Margin is treated as one input in an LR budget alongside **age, EIC, lobular histology, LVI and systemic therapy**. Pts re-excised to negative margins carry the same low LR as initially negative pts (Freedman), which favors re-excision when it is cosmetically cheap.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents women with invasive breast cancer or DCIS after lumpectomy with close or positive margins, planned for whole-breast RT. Does not represent DCIS managed without RT or pts already committed to mastectomy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Close margins sometimes show LR at or above positive margins (Fox Chase 10-yr **14% vs 12%**), pointing to selection and boost escalation confounding the margin effect. **No preference data** and no RCT inform the boost vs re-excision choice.

studies.interpretation:
The spine of this talk is an acceptability threshold rather than a margin threshold. If BCT matches mastectomy survival when in-breast relapse stays near 1%/yr or 10% at 10 yrs, then any margin policy is judged by whether it keeps a given patient under that line. That framing turns a pathology argument into a risk-budget argument, and it explains why the speaker ends at individualize rather than at a millimetre cutoff. A focally positive posterior margin in an older woman at high systemic risk spends little of the budget; a close margin in a woman under 40 with EIC may spend all of it.

The weakness is what sits under the budget. Nearly every margin-specific number comes from single-institution retrospective series (Fox Chase, Schnitt, IGR, Stanford, Tufts, Curie) using different definitions of close and positive, different boost doses, and re-excision decisions made by the treating team. Margin status in those series is not randomized; it travels with tumour size, EIC, age and surgeon. The Fox Chase data show the problem plainly: close margins carried 14% LR at 10 yrs against 12% for positive ones, an inversion that reads less like biology and more like selection plus boost dose escalated by margin category. The post hoc EORTC pathology review, in which margin status lost significance on MVA once age, grade and boost entered the model, points the same way.

The randomized evidence speaks to boost, not to re-excision. The EORTC boost trial in negative-margin pts showed 7.3% vs 4.3% LR at 5 yrs with a cosmetic cost (86% vs 71%), and EORTC 22881 in margin-positive pts showed a higher boost dose lowering LR at a steep fibrosis price. Neither tests re-excision against boost, and the speaker says so directly: no RCT on control or cosmesis for that comparison, and no patient preference data. MILAN II is offered as the closest proxy, but it compares quadrantectomy with tumourectomy plus an implant boost, which confounds extent of surgery with boost technique. The framework therefore substitutes a judgment about cosmesis for a trial that does not exist.

For a radiation oncologist the practical read is that boost is the tool the randomized evidence supports and re-excision is the tool the consensus prefers. The deck defines negative as >2 mm, a threshold the later SSO-ASTRO consensus for invasive disease replaced with no ink on tumour, so much of the close-margin category that drives this talk would now be managed with whole-breast RT and no further surgery. What stays durable is the risk-factor overlay (age, EIC, lobular histology, LVI, multiple involved margins, absent systemic therapy) and the point that an anterior margin of skin or a posterior margin of fascia leaves little room for residual disease.

What would make the framework wrong: if modern systemic therapy and imaging have compressed the LR gap between close and negative margins enough that even the young EIC-positive patient sits under 1%/yr, the re-excision mandate weakens further. The speaker's own caveat cuts the other way, that 5-yr LR may be premature when systemic therapy delays rather than prevents relapse, which argues for long follow-up before relaxing margin policy in the highest-risk group.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Boost dose trades against fibrosis: in EORTC 22881 margin-positive pts, LR was 17.5% with a 10 Gy boost vs 10.8% with 26 Gy, at severe fibrosis 3% vs 14%. That bounds how far a boost can stand in for re-excision before cosmesis is lost.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Residual disease on re-excision tracks margin extent: 30% focal, 45% minimal, 70% moderate, 85% extensive (Neuschatz). Re-excision to negative margins restores initially-negative LR (Freedman), while anterior skin-only or posterior fascia-only margins carry less need to re-excise.

open_questions: Re-excision vs RT boost for close or focally positive margins
Margin policy in pts under 40 with EIC in the modern era

presentation.speaker: Scott Tyldesley
presentation.summary: The speaker frames margin management as a risk budget: BCT matches mastectomy survival when in-breast relapse stays near 1%/yr or 10% at 10 yrs, so a margin matters to the extent it pushes a patient over that line. Close and positive margins raise LR in retrospective series, but no RCT compares re-excision with RT boost, and boost dose escalation buys control at a fibrosis and cosmesis cost. The framework re-excises grossly positive margins, and close or focally positive margins in young women with EIC, while accepting boost alone for older or high-systemic-risk pts and anterior or posterior margins. The bottom line is to individualize.
critique: Margin-specific LR figures rest on single-institution retrospective series with inconsistent close/positive definitions and boost doses escalated by margin category, so the margin effect is confounded with selection and dose.
No RCT compares re-excision with RT boost for control or cosmesis; the re-excision preference for close margins is consensus, and the speaker concedes its benefit is uncertain.
The >2 mm negative-margin definition predates the SSO-ASTRO no-ink-on-tumour consensus for invasive disease, which would treat most close margins here as adequate with whole-breast RT.
Most LR estimates come from eras before current systemic therapy, and the speaker notes 5-yr LR may be premature when systemic therapy only delays relapse.

studies.name: Using Oncotype DX for Radiotherapy Decisions in Breast Cancer
studies.tldr: Oncotype RS is prognostic for LRR in ER+ disease across retrospective trial subsets, but RT omission on RS alone belongs on trial, not in clinic.
details: 🔍 RS linked to LRR in node-negative NSABP B-14/B-20 (retrospective secondary analysis)
🔍 RS linked to LRR in node-positive NSABP B-28, all pts on chemo (retrospective secondary analysis)

details.text: 🔍 SWOG 8814 RS validation cohort (ER and/or PR+, node+, post-menopausal, tamoxifen ± CAF)
subdetails: Parent trial N = 1477; RS available from optional tumor banking, N = 367
Excluded: mastectomy + RT (37), BCS without RT (9), unknown surgery (5)
RS cutpoint of 18 chosen by exploratory analysis in the same data

details.text: 📐 LRR on multivariable analysis, SWOG 8814 RS subset
📊 LRR, mastectomy without RT, by RS

details: ⚠️ >3 LN+ after mastectomy: no RS separation (27% and 25.9%, p=0.27); nodal burden dominates
⚠️ BCT results not presented due to insufficient events, so the signal is mainly post-mastectomy without RT
🔗 EORTC 22922 IM-MS RT (50Gy): 15-yr breast cancer mortality 19.8% → 16.0% (p=0.006)
🔗 The speaker reads the EORTC 22922 benefit as independent of LRR, so an LRR-only biomarker may be too narrow

details.text: 🔍 Omission and de-escalation studies cited (open at time of talk)
subdetails: Tailor RT: N = 2140, ER+ with 1-3 positive nodes, RS <18, regional RT vs no regional RT
Tailor RT stratified by RS (0-10, 11-17); mastectomy pts in no-regional-RT arm get no RT
LUMINA: Canada, age 55+, unifocal stage I pN0, Luminal A by IHC (Ki67 not >13%), endocrine alone after BCS
PRECISION and IDEA (US): one uses Oncotype RS ≤18 (age 50-69), the other Prosigna PAM50 <40 + Luminal A (age 50-75)

details: 💊 The speaker's MD Anderson nodal RT algorithm uses genomic score as one factor alongside age, grade, LVSI, Ki-67 and tumor location
🔍 Also flagged: genomically personalized dose, RSI substituted into the LQ model
studies.significance: The usable RT signal is post-mastectomy without RT: RS 18+ vs 0-17 LRR 11.1% vs 1.5% in 1-3 LN+ (p=0.051), with no separation at >3 LN+ (p=0.27). That places RS inside the genuinely contested pN1 PMRT/RNI decision and out of the 4+ node decision, the same population Tailor RT tests.
studies.monday_clinic: In ER+ pN1 (1-3 nodes) after mastectomy, this supports counting a known high RS as one risk factor alongside age, grade and LVSI in the PMRT/RNI decision; it does not support omission on low RS alone.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: A talk dated November 11, 2018 synthesizing **retrospective secondary analyses** of NSABP B-14/B-20, B-28 and SWOG 8814, none of which randomized RT. The SWOG 8814 RS subset came from **optional tumor banking**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: SWOG 8814: **ER and/or PR+, node+, post-menopausal**, tamoxifen alone or with CAF. The analyzed cohort kept BCS + RT and **mastectomy without RT**, with mean age 60 yrs and median LRR follow-up 8.2 yrs.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The speaker set the RS-LRR data against EORTC 22922 and MA-20, where regional RT improved breast cancer outcomes **independent of LRR**. The de-escalation question moves to Tailor RT for pN1 and to LUMINA, PRECISION and IDEA for endocrine-alone after BCS.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents ER+ node-positive pts, chiefly post-mastectomy without RT in the tamoxifen ± CAF era. Does not represent pts treated with BCT, for whom events were too few to report.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The analyzed subset is defined by **who did not get RT**, which reflects referral patterns of the era. Univariate LRR did not differ by HER2, grade or age, so the RS signal is not cross-checked against the clinical factors the algorithm pairs it with.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: RS is **prognostic for LRR, not shown predictive of RT benefit**, which is why the speaker places it inside a multifactor algorithm rather than using it as an omission gate. Whether a low RS identifies pN1 pts who can skip regional RT is the open question Tailor RT was built to answer.

studies.interpretation:
The talk's core move is to repurpose a chemotherapy-selection assay as a locoregional risk tool, and the evidence offered points in one direction: three datasets from trials designed around systemic therapy each show higher-RS tumors recurring locoregionally more often. Consistency across NSABP B-14/B-20, B-28 and SWOG 8814 is the strongest part of the case, because together these span tamoxifen-only and chemotherapy-plus-tamoxifen populations and both node-negative and node-positive disease. What that consistency establishes is prognosis. None of these trials randomized RT, so the data cannot say whether a high-RS pt gains more from RT than a low-RS pt, which is the question a radiation oncologist is actually asking.

The SWOG 8814 analysis deserves a closer read because it carries the node-positive claim. The RS subset exists only because some sites banked tissue, the cohort was narrowed further by excluding pts who did receive post-mastectomy RT, and BCT outcomes were not presented for lack of events. The signal is therefore mostly a mastectomy-without-RT signal from an era of tamoxifen and older axillary practice. The cutpoint of 18 was chosen by exploratory analysis within the same data, and the multivariable RS hazard ratio has a lower confidence bound of 1.02, so the estimate is fragile and the threshold is at risk of being tuned to this cohort. In the >3 node mastectomy group RS did not separate outcomes, which is biologically sensible: when nodal burden already drives a high LRR, an expression score adds little.

The speaker's pivot to EORTC 22922 and MA-20 is the sharper argument, and it partly undercuts the LRR framing the first half builds. If regional RT reduces breast cancer mortality through a route not captured by locoregional recurrence counts, then a biomarker validated only against LRR could misclassify exactly the pts who benefit. That concern is fair, and it explains why the deck lands on trials rather than practice: Tailor RT asks whether regional RT can be dropped in ER+ pN1 with RS <18, while LUMINA, PRECISION and IDEA test endocrine therapy alone after BCS in biologically low-risk stage I disease.

The practical framework, folding a genomic score into a multifactor nodal RT algorithm rather than using it as a gate, is the defensible reading of this evidence. It lets RS tip an otherwise intermediate pN1 decision without carrying an omission decision on its own. What would make the framework wrong is a randomized result showing RS is prognostic but not predictive for RT benefit; in that case a high score argues for more systemic therapy, not larger fields, and a low score would not license dropping RT. The deck is dated 2018 and cites the omission studies as open, so it cannot speak to their readouts, and a reader should check those before leaning on RS in either direction.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: RS separated LRR only where nodal burden was modest: 11.1% vs 1.5% in 1-3 LN+ after mastectomy without RT (p=0.051), not at >3 LN+ (p=0.27). That makes it a tiebreaker for pN1 PMRT/RNI, while omission on low RS awaits Tailor RT.

open_questions: Does RS predict RT benefit, or only LRR risk?
Is regional RT omission safe in ER+ pN1 with RS <18?
Do endocrine-alone cohorts after BCS hold up with long f/u?

presentation.speaker: Wendy A. Woodward
presentation.summary: The speaker argued that the 21-gene RS, built to predict distant recurrence and chemo benefit, also tracks locoregional recurrence in ER+ disease, citing secondary analyses of B-14/B-20, B-28 and SWOG 8814. In the SWOG 8814 subset, RS 18+ predicted LRR on multivariable analysis alongside 4+ nodes. The speaker cautioned that the EORTC 22922 survival benefit was independent of LRR, so an LRR-only biomarker may be too narrow, and that omitting RT on RS alone belongs on trial. The proposed use is RS as one input among clinical factors in a nodal RT algorithm, not a standalone gate.
critique: Every RS-LRR dataset is a retrospective secondary analysis of a systemic-therapy trial; none randomized RT, so RS is shown to be prognostic for LRR, never predictive of RT benefit.

The SWOG 8814 cohort is 316 pts drawn from optional tumor banking within a 1477-pt trial, with BCT events too few to report, so selection and a mostly mastectomy-without-RT population shape the signal.
The cutpoint of 18 was found by exploratory analysis in the same data, and the RS hazard ratio's lower bound of 1.02 leaves the multivariable estimate fragile.
Tamoxifen-era cohorts with older axillary practice and no modern endocrine or nodal staging may overstate the LRR gap a contemporary pN1 pt faces.

studies.name: Radiation Therapy after Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy for Breast Cancer
studies.tldr: PMRT after NAC has no randomized basis; decide on pre-chemo clinical stage plus ypN status, using NSABP failure patterns and MDACC retrospective series.
details: 🔍 No RCT of PMRT after NAC: NSABP B-18 and B-27 prohibited PMRT
🔍 Framework built from NSABP patterns of failure plus MDACC institutional series

details.text: 📊 NSABP B-18/B-27 LRR without PMRT (Mamounas JCO 2012)
📊 NSABP MVA predictors of LRR
subdetails: Mastectomy: cT3+, cN+, ypT+, ypN+
BCS: same factors plus age <50
ypN+ with 1-3 positive nodes: LRR >10% (except cN0 ≥50yo with BCS)

details.text: ⚠️ NSABP caveats limit transfer to modern NAC
subdetails: No ER/PR/HER2 status
No N2 pts
Tamoxifen for all B-27 pts regardless of ER/PR status

details.text: 📊 MDACC 10-yr LRR by subgroup, non-randomized (542 PMRT vs 132 no PMRT; Huang JCO 2004)
📊 MDACC 10-yr CSS by subgroup (Huang JCO 2004)
📊 MDACC selected subsets: cT3N0 (Nagar IJROBP 2011) and age <35 (Garg IJROBP 2007)

details: ⚠️ Age <35 cohort: no OS or LRR benefit for clinical stage IIA

details.text: 🔍 Decision framework on the slides: MDACC vs UC Athena consensus

rows: cT3-T4; cN2-N3; most node-positive at resection
Clinical stage II with pN+, or high-risk features: age <35, ER, poor chemo response
<40yo; advanced clinical or pathologic stage and TNBC; LVI; ECE
Clinical stage II (T1N0-1, T2N0), >40yo, ER+, pCR or 0-3 positive nodes without LVI or ECE

details.text: 🔍 Axillary staging after NAC drives the ypN input
subdetails: ACOSOG Z1070 (n=687, cN1-2): nodal pCR 39%
Post-NAC SLNB FNR 12.6% for cN1
Axillary US alone: FNR 15%
SENTINA: repeat SLNB only 60% sensitive
Clip marking, dual tracer, >2 sentinel nodes lower FNR (NCCN 3.2015)

details: 🔍 Case: 53yo TNBC, 1/3 SLN micromet pre-NAC → AC-T → bilateral mastectomy + ALND, pCR; PMRT omitted
🔗 Pending at time of talk: NSABP B51/RTOG 1304, Alliance A11202, RAPCHEM (NCT01279304)
studies.significance: The PMRT call combines pre-chemo clinical stage and post-chemo nodal status; neither one decides it alone. Without PMRT, NSABP mastectomy LRR exceeded 10% with 1-3 ypN+ nodes, and MDACC cT3N0 pN+ ran 53% vs 5% 5-yr LRR without vs with PMRT. For cN1 converting to ypN0, the deck's evidence stops at consensus and pending B-51.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT1-2 disease with a proven node converting to ypN0 after NAC, this deck supports considering PMRT omission on consensus and non-randomized data only; it does not extend to cT3-T4, cN2-N3, or residual ypN+ disease, where MDACC series favor PMRT.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **No randomized PMRT data after NAC**: NSABP B-18 and B-27 prohibited PMRT. Indications are built from **NSABP patterns of failure** and **MDACC retrospective series**, keyed to pre-chemo clinical stage and post-chemo pathology.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: NSABP mastectomy pts without PMRT had **12.6% LRR**, and LRR exceeded **10%** with 1-3 ypN+ nodes. MDACC's **non-randomized** comparison (542 vs 132) showed lower 10-yr LRR with PMRT in cT3-T4, cN2/3 and ≥4 pN+.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents breast cancer pts after anthracycline/taxane NAC who are weighing PMRT on clinical stage and ypN status. Does not represent modern HER2-targeted or subtype-directed NAC cohorts, which the NSABP data predate.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: NSABP lacks ER/PR/HER2 status and N2 pts, and tamoxifen was given regardless of ER/PR. The case's positive node was excised by SLNB before NAC, so its ypN0 does not reflect nodal response.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The open zone is **cT1-2 cN1 converting to ypN0**. Here the deck offers consensus (UC Athena) and pending trials (B-51/RTOG 1304, A11202, RAPCHEM), not tested omission.

studies.interpretation:
The talk's core move is to accept that PMRT after neoadjuvant chemotherapy was never randomized, and to rebuild the question from the trials that forbade it. That is a sound strategy. NSABP B-18 and B-27 left chest walls unirradiated after mastectomy, so their locoregional failures are a clean natural history. The multivariable predictors that come out of them (clinical T3 or larger, clinical node positivity, residual breast disease, residual nodal disease, and age <50 after breast conservation) are the variables a radiation oncologist already has at consult. The weakness is the era. Those trials predate routine receptor testing and HER2-directed therapy, gave tamoxifen without regard to ER status, and excluded N2 disease. Their absolute LRR rates may be too high for some subtypes and too low for others. A TNBC pt with nodal pCR today differs in biology and systemic regimen from the average B-27 participant.

The MDACC series supply the other half: the effect of PMRT where it was given. Their signal is strongest where few now debate PMRT (cT4, cN2/3, ≥4 positive nodes at surgery), with CSS gains alongside LRR gains. These are non-randomized comparisons with a much smaller unirradiated group. In a referral cohort, the pts who did not get PMRT may have been selected for reasons tied to prognosis, in either direction. The cT3N0 and <35 subsets push the indication further, but they are small single-institution cuts, and the cT3N0 pN0 difference did not reach significance.

The framework is least certain about the case it chose to illustrate: clinical stage II, node positive before chemotherapy, converting to ypN0. For that group the deck offers only the UC Athena consensus and the NSABP finding that LRR stays modest, which is consensus and natural history rather than a tested omission. The case is also a weaker test than it looks. The involved node was a micrometastasis removed before chemotherapy, so its ypN0 status reflects surgery, not response. The axillary data matter here because the PMRT decision now depends on ypN. A post-NAC sentinel biopsy that misses residual disease feeds a false-negative straight into an omission decision.

B-51/RTOG 1304 was built to close that gap. It has since reported no recurrence benefit from adding regional nodal RT (with chest wall RT after mastectomy) in pts converting from cN1 to ypN0. That supports the direction the speaker took. But B-51 tested a selected population, and the subtype, residual-breast-disease and young-age modifiers the talk raises still lack randomized footing. Alliance A11202 addresses the other end, residual nodal disease, where the question is axillary RT as a substitute for dissection rather than whether to irradiate at all.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Without PMRT, NSABP mastectomy LRR exceeded 10% with 1-3 ypN+ nodes, and MDACC cT3N0 pN+ ran 53% vs 5% 5-yr LRR without vs with PMRT. So clinical stage and ypN status together set the indication. The cN1-to-ypN0 omission zone rests on consensus, not tested data.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: ypN status now gates the PMRT call, so axillary accuracy matters: post-NAC SLNB FNR was 12.6% for cN1 in ACOSOG Z1070, above the 10% threshold, and SENTINA repeat SLNB was only 60% sensitive. Clip marking, dual tracer and >2 sentinel nodes lower the FNR.

open_questions: PMRT omission in cN1 converting to ypN0
Axillary RT vs ALND for residual nodal disease after NAC
Does nodal pCR in TNBC justify omitting PMRT?

presentation.summary: The speaker argued that PMRT after neoadjuvant chemotherapy has no randomized basis, since NSABP B-18 and B-27 prohibited it, so the decision has to be built from patterns of failure and institutional series. NSABP data flag cT3+, cN+, ypT+ and ypN+ (plus age <50 after BCS) as LRR predictors. MDACC retrospective series show PMRT lowering LRR and improving CSS in cT3-T4, cN2/3 and heavily node-positive disease. The proposed framework: PMRT for advanced clinical stage or residual nodal disease, consideration for stage II with pN+ or young age, and omission for stage II pts reaching pCR, as in the illustrative TNBC case.
critique: Every recommendation rests on retrospective or secondary data; the MDACC PMRT comparison was non-randomized (542 vs 132), so pts who skipped PMRT may have been selected on prognostic features.
NSABP LRR baselines predate receptor testing and HER2-directed therapy, gave tamoxifen regardless of ER/PR and excluded N2, so their absolute risks may not transfer to subtype-directed NAC.
In the case, the only positive node was a micrometastasis excised by SLNB before NAC, so ypN0 after ALND does not measure nodal response, yet nodal pCR is what the omission rests on.
The deck predates the B-51/RTOG 1304 readout, which has since reported no invasive recurrence benefit from regional nodal RT in cN1 converting to ypN0; the framework should be re-read against it.

studies.name: pCR as a Surrogate Marker for Outcomes in Breast Cancer
studies.tldr: pCR after neoadjuvant chemo is strongly prognostic per pt but a weak trial-level surrogate; response should guide post-neoadjuvant systemic and locoregional tailoring.

details.text: 📊 CTNeoBC: pCR vs no pCR by pCR definition

details: ⚠️ CTNeoBC: magnitude of pCR improvement between arms did not predict EFS or OS effect

details.text: 🔍 The speaker's proposed reasons for the trial-level miss
subdetails: Low pCR rates
Heterogeneous populations
Few targeted therapies (NOAH the exception)
Larger between-arm pCR differences needed, possibly subtype-specific

details: 📊 NSABP B-27 (2411 pts): adding docetaxel raised pCR, yet DFS HR=0.86, p=0.10 (preop) and HR=0.91, p=0.27 (postop)
📊 ALTTO (N=6281): L+T v T DFS HR .84, P=0.048, short of the P < 0.025 threshold

details.text: 📊 GeparTrio pCR (ypT0 ypN0) by interim response, conventional vs response-guided

details: 🔗 GeparTrio: response-guided therapy improved survival with flat pCR; the benefit came from luminal tumors, whose prognosis does not depend on pCR

details.text: 💊 Post-neoadjuvant setting pitched as ideal for testing new agents
subdetails: Enrolls only high-risk residual disease, proven resistant to existing therapy
High event rate → small sample size, short f/u
KATHERINE: residual invasive tumor, T-DM1 vs Herceptin; radiation per standard guidance
Penelope (NSABP B-54-I): N=800 HR+/HER2- without pCR, CPS-EG score ≥3, palbociclib vs placebo

details: 🔍 Locoregional section: less axillary surgery and less XRT after downstaging, possible omission of surgery or XRT. No supporting data shown
studies.significance: The RT content is the closing section, where less locoregional XRT after primary and nodal downstaging, and possible omission, are listed as promises without recurrence data. GeparTrio's subtype split gates that decision: pCR is highly prognostic in HER2+ and triple-negative disease, while luminal prognosis does not depend on pCR, so ypN0 alone is a weak omission criterion.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: CTNeoBC compared three pCR definitions: ypT0 ypN0, **ypT0/is ypN0 (preferred FDA definition)**, and ypT0/is irrespective of nodal status. Ignoring nodal status weakened the association with EFS and OS.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: CTNeoBC supplies both the pooled patient-level association (**EFS HR=0.48, OS HR=0.36** for ypT0/is ypN0) and the **trial-level null**. NSABP B-27, ALTTO and GeparTrio are the worked examples of pCR and long-term outcome moving apart.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The working model is that pCR is **prognostic, not a validated surrogate**, and its prognostic weight depends on subtype: high in HER2+ and triple-negative disease, low in luminal tumors. Its practical use is triage after surgery, escalating systemic therapy for residual disease and, prospectively, de-escalating locoregional therapy after downstaging.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents early breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, where pCR is most informative in HER2+ and triple-negative disease. Does not represent luminal tumors, where the slides show prognosis does not depend on pCR.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The newest cited data are from ASCO 2014, and the post-neoadjuvant trials appear as **schemas without results**. The locoregional de-escalation section is aspirational, with no recurrence or pattern-of-failure data.

studies.interpretation:
The core distinction in this talk is between a prognostic marker and a surrogate endpoint, and the speaker's own evidence supports the first more cleanly than the title suggests. CTNeoBC shows that an individual pt who reaches pCR does better, and the association is stronger when nodal status is part of the definition, which matches the definition the FDA prefers. The same pooled analysis found that larger pCR gains between randomized arms did not predict larger EFS or OS gains. That result matters for drug development, and it argues against using pCR as a stand-in for survival in a trial, whatever its value at the bedside.

The worked examples show the disconnect running both ways. In NSABP B-27, adding docetaxel raised pCR without a convincing DFS difference. In HER2+ disease, dual blockade improved pCR in neoadjuvant trials, yet ALTTO missed the P < 0.025 threshold of its changed analysis plan, with an HR of .84. GeparTrio inverts the pattern: response-guided treatment barely moved pCR but improved survival, and the benefit came from luminal tumors, the subtype where pCR carries the least prognostic information. The takeaway is that pCR is informative where treatment effects act through eradicating chemosensitive disease, and uninformative where they do not.

The speaker's explanations for the trial-level failure (low pCR rates, heterogeneous populations, too few targeted agents) are plausible but untested within the deck, and the slide illustrating an ideal correlation uses simulated data. So the question a trialist needs answered, how large a pCR difference in which subtype predicts a survival difference, is still open at the end of the talk.

The constructive half of the argument is the post-neoadjuvant design. Residual disease after modern neoadjuvant therapy identifies a chemo-resistant, high-event cohort, so an adjuvant trial in that cohort can be small and fast. The logic is sound, and KATHERINE and Penelope are its test cases, but the deck shows them only as schemas. Their readouts postdate the cited data, and those readouts, not the framework alone, are what a reader should weigh.

For a radiation oncologist, the relevant section is the shortest. Reducing nodal RT after axillary downstaging, or omitting some locoregional therapy after pCR, is presented as a promise. Nothing in the deck addresses locoregional recurrence after pCR. Because pCR's prognostic weight depends on subtype, any omission rule would probably need to be subtype-specific rather than keyed to ypN0 alone. Until randomized locoregional data exist, pCR informs the discussion of nodal coverage but does not settle it.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Less locoregional XRT after primary and nodal downstaging, and possible omission, appear only as promises with no recurrence data. pCR is highly prognostic in HER2+ and triple-negative disease, while luminal prognosis does not depend on pCR, so ypN0 alone is a weak basis for omitting nodal RT.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: CTNeoBC found that pCR gains between arms did not predict EFS or OS effect, so a neoadjuvant pCR win is not a survival claim. Residual disease is pitched as the setting for escalation trials, with KATHERINE and Penelope shown as schemas only.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Converting inoperable tumors to operable ones and mastectomy candidates to breast conservation is framed as established. Less axillary surgery through SNB after nodal downstaging is listed as a promise, and the deck carries no regional recurrence data to support it.

open_questions: Magnitude of pCR gain needed to predict EFS/OS benefit, by subtype
Safe omission of nodal RT after ypN0 conversion
Optimal post-neoadjuvant therapy for residual disease by subtype

presentation.speaker: Terry Mamounas
presentation.summary: The speaker argues that pCR after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is strongly prognostic for the individual pt but an unreliable trial-level surrogate. CTNeoBC anchors the case: pCR tracks with EFS and OS, less tightly when nodal status is ignored, yet the size of a pCR gain between arms did not predict the survival effect. NSABP B-27, ALTTO and GeparTrio illustrate the disconnect in both directions, and GeparTrio ties pCR's prognostic weight to HER2+ and triple-negative disease. The proposed framework uses response to tailor what follows: escalated systemic therapy for residual disease in post-neoadjuvant trials and, prospectively, de-escalated surgery and radiotherapy after downstaging.
critique: The title frames pCR as a surrogate, but the speaker's own CTNeoBC slide shows pCR gains did not predict EFS or OS effect; the deck establishes patient-level prognosis, not trial-level surrogacy.

The offered reasons for that failure (low pCR rates, heterogeneity, larger differences needed) are untested hypotheses, and the correlation slide is simulated data, so the pCR gain that predicts benefit is never shown.

The locoregional promises (less axillary surgery, less XRT after downstaging, omitting some locoregional therapy) come with no locoregional recurrence data, so the talk gives no evidence on the RT omission question it raises.

The post-neoadjuvant argument rests on KATHERINE and Penelope shown as schemas only; with the newest cited data from ASCO 2014, the deck cannot show that escalation for residual disease improves outcomes.

studies.name: Treatment Planning Techniques for Larger Body Habitus Breast/Chestwall and Nodal RT
studies.tldr: In obese pts needing breast/chest wall plus nodal RT, escalate stepwise from 3D extended tangents to photon/electron mix, VMAT, or prone by anatomy and constraints.
details: 🔍 4 techniques for obese/extreme obese pts (weight range 225lbs-363lbs), breast/chest wall + regional nodal RT, 50Gy/25fractions

details.text: 🔍 Decision framework: which technique, when

rows: Simplest 3D total nodal plan; tangents clear contralateral breast yet cover IMN PTV
Add higher photon energy if >23cm separation; tangent 20cm or less in length
Contralateral breast in extended tangent, or ~4cm or greater lung in tangents
IMN depth less than ~5cm for 16e or less; IM electron field >3.5cm wide
Left side, heart mean dose target <5Gy
16e upper, 12e lower; 1cm matchline changes after 8th and 16th fraction
3D plans do not meet protocol dose constraints
ABC not currently used; may add esophagus, stomach, liver, airway ROIs
Pt must tolerate >30 minutes on table

details: 🔍 Sim: supine on wing board, custom vac-bag, both arms up, head turned contralateral
📊 ABC breath hold: 46.7% increase in ipsilateral lung volume (1077cc vs 1580cc) in one example
🔍 Extended tangents: isocenter ~1-2cm from lateral chest wall; 6x/18x for separations larger than ~23cm
📊 Split-energy IMC electrons (16e upper, 12e lower) held heart mean dose at 4.12Gy
📊 VMAT example: lower ipsilateral lung dose than photon/electron mix, at the cost of higher heart dose
⚠️ Prone left total nodal plan left inferior IMNs uncovered, heart dose prioritized
⚠️ Photon/electron first-day imaging plus treatment timeline ran 16min 20secs
⚠️ No toxicity or locoregional control data; every comparison is a single-case plan example
studies.significance: The usable content is the set of switch points: tangents stay 3D until separation exceeds ~23cm (add 18x) or ~4cm or more of lung enters the field, electron IMN fields work only when nodes sit less than ~5cm deep, and VMAT is reserved for 3D plans failing B51/RTOG 1304 constraints. ABC added 46.7% ipsilateral lung volume in one example.
studies.monday_clinic: In an obese pt needing breast or chest wall plus regional nodal RT at 50Gy/25fractions, this supports starting with 3D tangents or a photon/electron mix and moving to VMAT only on constraint failure; it does not address hypofractionated nodal regimens or proton planning.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Single-institution (Virginia Commonwealth University) planning talk built on worked case examples. **All cases obese/extreme obese**, weight range 225lbs-363lbs. No outcome cohort.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **50Gy/25fractions**, RTOG Breast Cancer Atlas contours, **NSABP B51/RTOG 1304** dose constraints. Supine on a wing board in a custom vac-bag, arms up; ABC deep-inhale breath hold checked with three reproducibility scans at CT.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Plans are judged against the B51/RTOG 1304 constraint set rather than institution-specific limits. The talk offers no comparison to published dosimetry or outcomes in obese cohorts.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents obese/extreme obese pts receiving breast or chest wall plus regional nodal RT at 50Gy/25fractions. Does not represent hypofractionated nodal regimens or proton planning.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Thresholds reflect one institution's practice without stated derivation. The prone example **left inferior IMNs uncovered** to protect the heart, a coverage compromise the talk does not quantify.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The contribution is the **escalation order** and the anatomic triggers between techniques. Whether VMAT's lower ipsilateral lung dose justifies its higher heart dose, and whether breath hold with arcs removes that trade, stays open.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The usable content is the set of switch points: tangents stay 3D until separation exceeds ~23cm (add 18x) or ~4cm or more of lung enters the field, electron IMN fields work only when nodes sit less than ~5cm deep, and VMAT is reserved for 3D plans failing B51/RTOG 1304 constraints.

open_questions: Dosimetric gain of VMAT vs 3D across an obese cohort, not single cases?
Can ABC breath hold be combined with arc planning in obese pts?
Toxicity and nodal control with prone total nodal plans omitting inferior IMNs?

presentation.speaker: Ruth Ann M. Good
presentation.summary: The speaker presented a single-institution planning playbook for breast/chest wall and regional nodal RT in obese pts (225lbs-363lbs) at 50Gy/25fractions, judged against B51/RTOG 1304 dose constraints. The framework escalates by anatomy: single-isocenter extended tangents first, a photon/electron mix with an electron IMN field when the contralateral breast or too much lung enters the tangents, VMAT when 3D plans fail protocol constraints, and prone positioning for very pendulous breasts. ABC breath hold is used to cut lung and heart dose on 3D plans. Each step rests on worked case examples with DVHs, not on outcome data.
critique: Every recommendation rests on single-case plan examples from one institution; no cohort dosimetry, toxicity, or locoregional control data support choosing one technique over another.
Switch thresholds (separation >23cm, lung ~4cm or greater, IMN depth less than ~5cm, electron width >3.5cm) are presented as rules without stated derivation or validation in a larger series.
The VMAT example trades lower ipsilateral lung dose for higher heart dose, and ABC is not currently used with arcs; whether breath hold with arcs removes that trade is left untested.
Proton therapy, an option for nodal RT when heart and lung constraints conflict, is not discussed, nor is hypofractionated nodal RT in this population.
